content.comment_body: Hello, How can I manage my digital outputs on [product_name] using a [product_name] controller? Is it possible to access the physical address of [product_name] directly from [product_name]? The connection between the two devices is already established. I just want to know how to reference the outputs on [product_name]. Thanks, [user_name]

You can write directly to the outputs of [product_name] only if the outputs are not used within the [product_name] program. If they are used in the program logic, the program will override any external control.

Thank you, [user_name]. I am not using the outputs in the [product_name] program, so the outputs act like an extended digital output module. How can I reference this digital output address? I've assigned a bit memory area in [product_name]. I'm looking for information on how to map this bit memory to the digital outputs of [product_name]. Thanks, [user_name]
Understood. Sometimes I forget how to reference individual bits within a byte. The issue is resolved now and it works correctly. Thanks again, [user_name].

If [product_name] is set up as a client and [product_name] as a server, digital outputs of one unit can be switched through inputs without a program in either device. This requires making the relevant entry in [product_name]'s connection list. For example: I0.0 to I0.7 of [product_name] switch outputs Q0.0 to Q0.7 of [product_name]. The same mapping applies in reverse.

That's exactly what I did. I initially started this discussion because I was unsure about the memory area for [product_name] outputs, and later realized that bits within each byte can be referenced directly. Thanks again, [user_name].
Alternatively, create a DB1 in [product_name] and write at addresses DB1.DBX1064.0 - DB1.DBX1066.3 to control Q1-Q20 in [product_name].
